title: Preflight: Cost Surge Simulation and Ops Cartography
summary: Runbook-oriented preflight covering a simulated 2x-5x cost/traffic surge, mapping service dependencies (ops cartography), and defining gating and rollback criteria for the upcoming regional rollout. Decisions: use 2x baseline sim first, instrument KV cache + prefix cache metrics, run golden-path smoke + extended soak, and prepare two rollback levels (degrade QoS then redirect to compatible model variants).
topics: Instrumentation gaps (KV cache / prefix cache / batching)
Retention and observability tradeoffs during surge
Who owns runbook steps and due dates
action_items: Owen Garcia: run 2x traffic cost surge sim with current autoscale policy and collect token-level cost breakdown - due 2026-01-13
Jordan Lee: produce ops cartography diagram (dep map + critical paths) and mark hot/warm/cold services - due 2026-01-11
Samir Desai: add KV cache hit-rate and prefix cache latency to per-route dashboards; add alert if miss-rate > 15% - due 2026-01-12
Priya Nair: write canary acceptance criteria doc and fallback messaging matrix for product - due 2026-01-14
Maya Patel: coordinate cross-team tabletop and send calendar invite for 2026-01-15 simulation review - due 2026-01-10
next_steps: Schedule 2x surge run and soak window
Lock three rollback tiers and test them in staging
Draft post-sim findings and cost mitigation recommendations
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-09 09:30 PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Owen, Jordan, Priya, Samir, Ethan, Rachel, Lena, Tom

Summary (auto): Preflight sim to validate cost and reliability under surge; produce ops dependency map and finalize rollback gating.

[00:00] Maya: okay let's get started um, thanks everyone for joining the preflight, I know it's early. main goals today are to agree the simulation parameters for cost/traffic surge and to produce an ops cartography so we know where to look when things go sideways.
[00:22] Owen: yep, and, uh, to confirm what metrics we use. token-level, per-route, prefix cache hit, kv cash — sorry K-V cash, kv cache — yes, that one.
[00:35] Jordan: also want to highlight sequencing: if prefix cache misses spike we'll see CPU blow for the runtime and latency climbs then autoscaler kicks which costs more. we need to map those dependencies.
[00:50] Priya: timeline constraint: product wants regional rollout in three weeks assuming preflight is green. so we can't have a month-long back-and-forth. we need a quick, actionable sim that surfaces the big risks.
[01:08] Samir: Agreed. My recommendation is start at 2x sustained qps for a 2 hour soak, then a 5x short spike for 10 minutes to exercise autoscaler path. we instrument model variants and quantization paths separately because quant-skew may show up.
[01:30] Ethan: from eng mgmt perspective, two asks: 1) how confident are we we can rollback to a lower-cost model variant without user-visible regressions, 2) what's our SLA exposure if we degrade QoS?
[01:44] Rachel: and ops needs clarity on audit logs — if we divert traffic or change quantization at runtime we need a clean audit trail for later review.
[01:53] Lena: retention question: during the sim can we reduce observability retention windows to save cost so the sim doesn't itself blow metrics storage?
[02:05] Owen: good point. we can temporarily lower retention, but we should ensure we still capture the critical windows. maybe downsample older buckets but keep raw during the two hour soak.
[02:20] Tom: also confirm canary criteria: do we require steady token latency under P95 thresholds and no regression in correctness for the sampled prompts? or is it okay to accept some degradation so long as user freeze isn't catastrophic?
[02:36] Maya: we need tiers: green (no action), amber (degrade QoS path), red (immediate redirect to backup model/region). define thresholds per route. Priya you can own the thresholds?
[02:49] Priya: yes, I'll draft thresholds. suggest start with P95 latency + token cost per request increase > 30% as amber.
[03:02] Jordan: back to ops cartography: I'll draw the dependency map showing runtime -> kv cache -> model variant store -> storage backend -> auth (SSO) because if auth latency spikes, requests pile up. also show observability pipeline and retention knobs.
[03:20] Samir: small transcription quirk: when we talk about kv cache, sometimes logs say 'k v cash' which confuses downstream tooling. we should normalize labels.
[03:34] Owen: action item: add a metric for prefix-cache-stale evictions and expose it per-route. if eviction rate > 5% for two consecutive windows we alert.
[03:48] Maya: what's the cost sim input set? Samir?
[03:52] Samir: we'll reuse the two canonical workloads: short chat bursts (64-128 tokens) and long form completions (512+ tokens). mix ratio 70/30 chat/completions for baseline. run with current autoscale policy and then with an aggressive policy to see delta. include cold-start penalty for private deployments.
[04:15] Ethan: include an experiment with reduced quantization on a small percent of traffic to see accuracy vs cost tradeoff. note that Anthropic's docs suggested similar approach but that's a different environment.
[04:32] Rachel: any competitor telemetry we should look at? not deep dive, but artifacts from OpenAI or Anthropic about fallback patterns.
[04:40] Priya: I'll dig up past notes from the 2025-11 rollout prep, there were some useful canary decision trees.
[04:50] [05:00] Jordan: question about scoring: when we redirect, do we do full redirect or partial weighted traffic? partial is safer but messier operationally.
[05:12] Owen: prefer two-step rollback: first degrade QoS (shorten response length, increase sampling temp—meaning lower compute) and drop to a cheaper model variant; second step full redirect to a different region or dedicated pool. full redirect should be last resort.
[05:28] Maya: good. document two rollback levels: degrade then redirect. Samir, can you prototype degrade behavior in staging?
[05:36] Samir: yes, I'll run a staged degrade and measure failure modes. need access to canary config toggles in staging.
[05:44] Tom: on instrumentation, we need token-level billing correlation. it's painful to reconcile tokens to cost today.
[05:52] Jordan: we're working on token-level breakdown per route, but we need to ensure the console shows it alongside latency. Owen can we extract token cost over time?
[06:02] Owen: yes, we'll add per-route token-cost series and a derived metric cost-per-1000-requests.
[06:10] [06:30] Priya: quick decision: run 2x sim first, if that looks ok then run 5x spike. does anyone object?
[06:40] Group: no objections.
[06:43] [07:00] Maya: parity check — who will publish ops cartography? Jordan?
[07:05] Jordan: yes I'll own the diagram. will mark critical paths and annotate owners.
[07:12] Maya: make sure to call out the observability gaps we flagged: kv label normalizing, token-cost mapping, prefix cache eviction metric, retention window for sim, and canary toggles.
[07:28] Lena: quick note — if we reduce retention during sim, downstream alerting like anomalies may trigger noisy pages. we'll quiet non-critical alerts for the window.
[07:38] Owen: I'll add an alert suppression window but keep critical SLO pages live.
[07:46] [08:00] Samir: something to watch: quantization skew. when we switch to int8 p8 or similar paths, outputs can change and evals may flag regressions. need a small evaluation harness to sample correctness on golden prompt set during the sim.
[08:18] Priya: good call. add that to the canary acceptance checklist.
[08:25] Maya: can we put owners on each canary check? yes.
[08:30] [08:45] Action item recap: Maya read the list out loud (paraphrased).
[08:50] Owen: I'll schedule the surge run and share the dashboard link.
[08:56] Jordan: I'll post the ops cartography in the doc and slack channel.
[09:02] Samir: staging toggles will be ready by Friday.
[09:08] Priya: thresholds doc will be in PR by Thursday.
[09:12] Maya: follow up tabletop for simulation review on 2026-01-15.
[09:18] [10:00] Ethan: one last question — during surge do we allow degrade paths that increase error rates slightly to protect latency? how do we quantify acceptable error?
[10:28] Rachel: product side says small precision tradeoffs are acceptable for non-critical routes; we'll mark which routes are critical.
[10:40] Maya: okay wrap up. I'll send meeting notes and owners. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript contains natural disfluencies, occasional mis-transcriptions ("K-V cash"), and some speaker overlap.
